_note: The UI JUSTIFICATION STORE (BL-260). One entry per information surface.
THE RULE (Ben, 2026-08-01): every UI element declares the QUESTION it answers and
WHY it earns its space. The pair is REQUIRED, not optional. Enforcement is
AUTHORSHIP, not machinery: 'the docs are the audit, we don't need an audit method
or arbitrary resolution.' No headless check, no report-only verify pass, is to be
built against this file. A surface without a justification is a defect a human
notices by READING the store -- which is the point of the store existing.
PROVENANCE (Ben's addition): each entry names the backlog item that DEMANDED the
surface, making this a two-way index --
surface -> item : why does this exist, and what asked for it.
item -> surface : what did this item actually put on screen.
It therefore exposes two gaps neither backlog.json nor user_stories.json can show:
a surface no item ever demanded (unjustified UI), and an item that claims a UI
outcome but owns no surface. Same coverage argument USER_STORIES.md makes on the
INTENT axis, applied to the SURFACE axis.
STATUS FIELD -- and why it exists:
settled : the wording is Ben's, or he has accepted it.
drafted : written BY an implementer FOR Ben to accept or rewrite. BL-260 is
explicit that the backfill text is Ben's to author, because writing
the pair IS the design check BL-247 named -- an implementer can build
the store and draft the text, but must not invent it and call it
settled. Every 'drafted' entry is an open question wearing a sentence.
NO RUNTIME CONSUMER, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. BL-247's in-UI question log
(the per-chart 'Answers/Because' toggle) was REMOVED 2026-08-02 (NR-018), so there
is no why_note() seam and no C++ call site left to feed. This store is therefore a
DOCUMENTATION artifact, which is exactly what 'the docs are the audit' asks for.
If a runtime consumer ever returns, the codegen seam Ben chose on 2026-08-09 (a
generated header of string literals, so a missing entry is a BUILD failure) is the
settled way to feed it -- recorded here so the decision is not re-litigated.
VIEW: docs/ui/QUESTION_LOG.md, generated by tools/session/render_question_log.js.
Never hand-edit the mirror.

market_ledger.answers: What is this good worth here, and who is willing to trade it?
market_ledger.because: Markets are the public intelligence channel under the BL-068 visibility rule -- a rival's production and stockpiles are private, so price and the order book are the only honest read the player has on a competitor. Without this surface the discovery model has no channel to reason through.

balance_ledger.answers: Where is my money going, and how long do I have?
balance_ledger.because: apply_budget nets six flows into one number; a single balance tells the player they are losing without telling them what to change. Itemising income, expenditure, maintenance, wages, interest and levies is what makes bankruptcy something to act on rather than discover. BL-343 added the Laws section beneath the policy levers: the first law that is not a stub sits directly under the two that are, so the difference between a drawn lever and a working one is visible in one glance.

construction_panel.answers: Can I build here, what will it cost me, and why was I refused?
construction_panel.because: Placement carries terrain, deposit, slot and now logistics-reach rules (BL-323). A refusal the player cannot read is indistinguishable from a broken build, so the panel must state the reason, not merely deny.

tile_inspector.answers: What is this ground, and what could it support?
tile_inspector.because: Terrain is two axes plus a deposit profile, none of which is fully legible from the canvas colour alone. Siting is the player's central recurring decision and this is where its inputs are read.

tech_tree_panel.answers: What can I unlock, and what stands between me and it?
tech_tree_panel.because: A constellation of gates is only a decision if the player can see which are reachable. BL-344 made that second half real: each node now reports EARNED, LOCKED with its unmet conditions itemised, or -- honestly -- "no gate authored", instead of showing an unevaluable string condition that could never resolve.

profile_panel.answers: Who am I in this world?
profile_panel.because: Identity is carried by emblem and colour across every canvas and ledger (BL-090). One place has to establish that vocabulary, or the marker colours are arbitrary everywhere else.

chat_panel.answers: What has happened that I did not watch happen?
chat_panel.because: The simulation runs while the player is looking elsewhere. Without a log, events are only discoverable by noticing a changed number, which is the failure mode the alerts work (BL-261) also targets.

header_panel.answers: Am I solvent, and what is the date?
header_panel.because: The two facts that condition every other decision, needed at a glance without opening anything. Runway (BL-073) is here rather than in the ledger precisely because it is a warning, not an analysis.

hover_card.answers: What is this thing I am pointing at?
hover_card.because: The canvas carries markers, glyphs and lens fills whose meaning is positional. Hover is the cheapest possible disclosure -- it answers without costing a click or displacing the current view, and glance-then-stick (BL-230) keeps it readable.

nav_pane.answers: What can I open from here?
nav_pane.because: Every ledger and panel needs exactly one discoverable door. BL-292 is the standing proof of the cost when a surface lacks one: the Economy panel was drawn every frame and reachable by nobody.

entity_summary.answers: What is this entity, in one line?
entity_summary.because: The shared per-entity content builder feeding the Selection element, the Tile Ledger and the hover card. It exists once so those three cannot drift into describing the same entity differently.

selection_panel.answers: What have I selected, and what can I do with it?
selection_panel.because: The pinned, polymorphic detail surface for the current selection. It is the answer to the click model's promise: single-click selects, and something must visibly happen when it does.

corporation_dashboard.answers: How is my corporation doing overall?
corporation_dashboard.because: Roll-up cards over holdings, balance and production, so the player has a whole-corp read without assembling it from four ledgers. Pairs existed on these cards before BL-247's log was removed. BL-343 added the sixth Finance bar, Levies: a law the player cannot see working is indistinguishable from an unimplemented one, so the levy is its own number rather than folded into maintenance.

selection_card.answers: Can I keep this detail on screen while I look at something else?
selection_card.because: Comparison is impossible when every selection replaces the last. The card frame is what makes drill-through (BL-214) a shared idiom rather than a per-panel behaviour. Pairs existed here before BL-247's log was removed.

generation_charts.answers: Why did this world come out the way it did?
generation_charts.because: Each chain stage settles one question about the body's history; the chart row is that stage's evidence. This surface carried the original BL-247 question pairs, which is why its per-round `question` field survives in generation_charts.hpp.

economy_panel.answers: How do the corporations, their holdings and the markets compare against each other?
economy_panel.because: The cross-corp comparison view. Ben ruled 2026-08-09 that it earns a nav-rail door rather than retirement (BL-292), so it must now justify the slot it occupies.

generation_ledger_body.surface: Generation Ledger - Body view (histograms, thresholds, profile echo)
generation_ledger_body.answers: What shape did this body's generation actually come out, and which input made it that shape?
generation_ledger_body.because: A biome-balance question ('forest and wetland stay sparse on the homeworld') was previously answered by eyeballing the map, which cannot distinguish a bad tuning constant from an unlucky seed. Putting the composition/landform histograms, the ocean threshold against the profile's target, and the profile that drove them on ONE surface is what makes the answer traceable to an input rather than to an impression. It earns its space as a tuning instrument, not shipped chrome - it is the last rail slot for that reason.

generation_ledger_tile.answers: Why is THIS tile what it is?
generation_ledger_tile.because: The six-pass pipeline discards its intermediates, so a surprising tile was previously unanswerable without a debugger: the heightmap, the sea score it was tested against, the moisture and the band all vanish before the tile exists. The breadcrumb names the input value and the rule that fired at each pass, which turns 'that looks wrong' into a specific pass to go and read. It is also the shared content builder the hover card and the Selection element are intended to wrap, so the space it earns is paid for more than once.

decision_feed.answers: What did the rival corporations just decide, and how close was the call?
decision_feed.because: The scorer has recorded its own rationale since BL-202 - the winning score, the runner-up score and a reason code, into a 256-entry ring and permanently into the history log - and nothing has ever read either store. The reasoning accumulated every tick of every session and was shown to nobody. The margin is what earns the space: a command taken at 0.81 against a runner-up of 0.79 is a coin-flip the tuning could have gone either way on, one taken at 0.90 against 0.10 is a conviction, and nothing else in the game distinguishes them. That difference is most of what 'which strategy is it running' means. It also pays as diagnostics rather than spectacle (AI_OPPONENT.md 10h): the idle/resume oscillation that was the AI's dominant behaviour for an unknown number of sprints was invisible for exactly this reason.
